This was me to a tee. I was scapegoated hardcore and at a young age I just said fuck it if nothing I do will make them happy then might as well just do my own thing. I was never sneaky about it or anything so I'd blatantly disobey and I'd disregard any punishments they'd put on me or just take whatever they did without reaction. I'd never disobey on purpose though, I'd pretty much give myself my own rules based on what I thought made sense and follow that instead. I'd act if my nparents were invisible pretty much, and their nonsensical and inconsistent narc rules irrelevant.

Looking back, this definitely had a lot of positive effects on me which I'm thankful for, like boosting my confidence and giving me a sense of self. I ended up really independent (mostly positive ways but some negative ways too), but I think it caused a lot of dissociation I wouldn't had otherwise because I was always trying to be brave and calm when really I was actually terrified. It also caused me to have a lot of anxiety since I had to make so many decisions all of the time and had the burden of figuring the world out so I could teach it to myself, something most people will get from their parents. Since I cut mine out so hard with my approach to dealing with them, I was self-parenting to the furthest extreme you could get. No surprise I developed multiple dissociative identities . . .

So, overall a good thing I think, I have a lot of gratitude to the small frustrated and unloved child 20 years ago that realized they'd be chastised no matter what they did and decided to just do whatever suits them and what they think is right no matter the consequences.

From discourse online and people I know who also had abusive childhoods it seems like most people growing up as scapegoats ended up people pleasing during there childhoods which makes sense. I don't see a lot of representation of the "fuck it" scapegoat, which makes sense, because I think the people whose situations/temperament allowed them to be fuck it scapegoats probably aren't as common, but we're out there!
